correctness.rationale: Concatenation gives superadditivity in n at each fixed d. Greedy embedding of a fixed target is equivalent to embedding by any index sequence, and after each first hit the remaining i.i.d. stream is independent, so successive waiting times are independent Geom(pᵢ) variables on {1,2,…}. Their negative Laplace transforms are Mᵢ(t) as stated. Markov's inequality and independence across sources give an e^{dtn} factor; summing over all length-ℓ targets gives exactly S_d(t)^ℓ. Choosing any fraction above dt/(−log S_d) gives vanishing tails and the finite-d bound. With t_d=log d/(dΔ), the nonmaximal-letter terms relative to the maximal one total O(1/d), including a tie among second-largest letters. Also Λ₁=t/p₁−(1−p₁)t²/(2p₁²)+O(t³), so the finite-d bound at t_d is p₁+(1−p₁)t_d/2+O(t_d²+1/(d log d)). The minimum of the d mode-letter counts yields the lower baseline by the strong law at fixed d. The limiting inequality is one-sided and does not assert sharpness or an asymptotic equivalent. value.rationale: The finite-d upper bound keeps the entire letter law and can be optimized by a one-variable search without calculating any subsequence probabilities. Its quantified strict-bias implication is substantially smaller than the benchmark order in the tied, uniform binary case and describes a meaningful distributional distinction. Credit is for the upper bound and usable variational expression, not an optimal rate or optimum coefficient.
